explanation: A temporary holy place where the Israelites worshiped God during their wilderness journey.
Poles used to carry the tabernacle when the Israelites moved camp.
The highest religious leader among the Israelites, responsible for performing sacrifices and other ceremonies.
Instruments made of silver that were used to call the assembly together and signal the movement of the camp.
The period during which the Israelites wandered in the wilderness after leaving Egypt and before entering the promised land.
A manifestation of God's presence that led the Israelites through the wilderness.
